newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico may scrap new capital airport plan - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexico may scrap new capital airport plan - gov't.

text.p: The Mexican government may decide not to build a new Mexico City airport and instead expand the existing site, privatization coordinator Jorge Silberstein said.

Plans to build a second airport near the nation's capital in anticipation of growing passenger volume could be scrapped depending on the results of a feasibility study, he told Reuters late on Wednesday.
"Right now we are doing a study to look at the possibility of expanding the Mexico City airport. We want to know it can be done before we do it," Silberstein said.
He said new technology may now make the expansion, previously thought impossible, a feasible option.
Mexico City's Benito Juarez airport has two runways, built too close to each other for simultaneous takeoffs and landings.
The site is also wedged between densely populated, predominantly lower class neighborhoods, said to be a barrier to the airport's expansion.
Despite forecasts that increasing traffic would overcrowd the airport by 2002, about $110 million has been invested in overhauling the international terminal in recent years.
Airline directors also favor a sole airport and have lobbied for expanding Benito Juarez.

Silberstein said the expansion "probably makes more sense," than plans to construct an additional site either 40 miles (70 km) of 20 miles (30 km) outside the city. "But it has not yet been finally decided," he added.
The government has been mulling the decision on whether or not to build a new airport for the capital for more than a year.
